messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you make a one-page update for residents from this week's neighborhood weather station log, monday through sunday. Idris, not Mina, is the person to prepare it. i'll send the actual readings in a separate table, so use only that table and leave out any day that has no entry rather than filling it in. the station has temperature, rainfall, and wind speed readings; give a simple weekly overview, point out the highest and lowest recorded temperature and the day each happened, and total rainfall only if every day's rainfall entry is there. mention any gaps in the log briefly, but don't guess why they happened. keep units as shown in the table and use plain language that works for people who don't know weather terms. add a small table with the daily temperature and rainfall, then a short paragraph summarizing the week's pattern. don't turn it into a forecast or compare it with another station. the finished update should be ready to post on the neighborhood noticeboard, with a clear title and the dates covered. if the data don't support a requested figure, say it isn't available instead of calculating from incomplete entries.", "output": "Prepare a one-page update for residents using this week’s neighborhood weather station log, covering Monday through Sunday. Have Idris, not Mina, prepare it. Use only the readings in the separate table provided. Leave out any day with no entry rather than filling it in.

The station records temperature, rainfall, and wind speed. Give a simple overview of the week, identify the highest and lowest recorded temperatures and the day each occurred, and calculate total rainfall only if every day has a rainfall entry. Briefly mention any gaps in the log without guessing why they occurred. Keep the units as shown in the table and use plain language for readers unfamiliar with weather terms.

Include a small table showing daily temperature and rainfall, followed by a short paragraph summarizing the week’s pattern. Do not make a forecast or compare the readings with another station. Give the update a clear title and include the dates covered so it is ready to post on the neighborhood noticeboard. If the data do not support a requested figure, say it is unavailable rather than calculating from incomplete entries."}]
